task.title: External CRM Integration - Salesforce Connector
task.description: Build the first external system integration to fulfill Renzo's core vision as a 'plug-and-play outreach intelligence layer'. Implement a Salesforce connector that: (1) OAuth 2.0 authentication flow with Salesforce (store refresh tokens securely in localStorage with encryption), (2) Settings page with 'Connect to Salesforce' button and connection status indicator, (3) One-way sync that pulls Accounts and Contacts from Salesforce into Renzo's contact database (map Salesforce fields: Account.Name→company, Contact.Email→email, Contact.Phone→phone, Account.AnnualRevenue→revenue, Contract.EndDate→contractExpiry, Account.LastActivityDate→lastContactDate), (4) Manual 'Sync Now' button that fetches updated data and merges with existing contacts (match on email, update if Salesforce data is newer), (5) Sync status dashboard showing last sync time, number of contacts synced, any errors, (6) Field mapping configuration UI allowing users to customize which Salesforce fields map to which Renzo fields, (7) Conflict resolution strategy (Salesforce wins vs. Renzo wins vs. manual review) selectable per field, (8) Sync log showing history of all sync operations with timestamps and records affected. Store Salesforce record IDs with each contact to enable future two-way sync. Add 'Connected Systems' section to Settings showing all active integrations. This establishes the integration architecture pattern for future connectors (Gmail, HubSpot, etc.).
task.rationale: This is the single most critical feature because the project description explicitly states Renzo should be 'a standalone app that can connect to external systems (Salesforce, Gmail, CRMs) via APIs' and the vision is 'a plug-and-play outreach intelligence layer that works with any existing business system without requiring migration'. Currently, Renzo only works with manually added or CSV-imported contacts, which contradicts its core value proposition. Building Salesforce integration first makes strategic sense because: (1) Salesforce is the dominant B2B CRM (19.8% market share), (2) it validates the integration architecture for future connectors, (3) it immediately unlocks the product's primary use case for B2B sales teams who already have their data in Salesforce, (4) it transforms Renzo from a basic contact manager into the intelligent layer it's meant to be. Without this, Renzo cannot fulfill its stated purpose of working 'with any existing business system'.

issues: CRITICAL: Hardcoded Salesforce client credentials exposed in frontend code - OAuth client secrets MUST be server-side only. Move all OAuth flows to backend API endpoints.

CRITICAL: Token storage uses weak base64 encoding (btoa) instead of proper encryption, storing sensitive OAuth tokens in localStorage accessible to any XSS attack. Implement httpOnly secure cookies via backend.
CRITICAL: Missing CSRF protection for OAuth callback and form submissions. Implement anti-CSRF tokens and validate OAuth state parameter server-side, not in sessionStorage which persists across tabs.
data.feedback: This implementation has fundamental security architecture flaws that make it unsuitable for production. IMMEDIATE FIXES REQUIRED: 1) Move ALL OAuth logic to backend - frontend should only redirect to your server's /auth/salesforce endpoint which handles client_secret securely. 2) Never store tokens in localStorage - use httpOnly secure cookies set by your backend after OAuth completion. 3) Implement proper CSRF protection using synchronizer tokens validated server-side. 4) Add token refresh logic in backend middleware to automatically renew expired tokens. 5) Remove inline styles and external font CDN to enable strict CSP headers. 6) Add input validation, rate limiting, and proper error handling on both frontend and backend. 7) Implement visual feedback for loading states, drag-drop zones, and keyboard accessibility. The 21KB of code shows effort but the OAuth implementation violates basic security principles - this would expose user credentials and allow account takeover. Redesign with security-first backend architecture before any frontend polish.

issues: Critical Security: No input validation/sanitization, missing CSRF protection, and XSS vulnerabilities - all user inputs in saveFieldMappings(), testConnection(), and sync operations lack validation before API calls
Incomplete Implementation: AppState object is cut off mid-declaration and authentication/token management is completely missing - application cannot function securely
CSP Violations: Content Security Policy uses 'unsafe-inline' for styles due to inline CSS throughout HTML, and missing img-src/other directives create security gaps
data.feedback: CRITICAL FIXES REQUIRED: 1) Implement input validation library (e.g., DOMPurify for XSS, validator.js for format checks) before all API calls - validate mappings object structure, sanitize CRM URLs/credentials. 2) Complete the AppState object declaration and add authentication flow with secure token storage (httpOnly cookies or encrypted sessionStorage). 3) Add CSRF token generation/validation to all state-changing operations. 4) Move all inline styles to external CSS file and remove 'unsafe-inline' from CSP. 5) Add rate limiting (e.g., debounce saveFieldMappings to 500ms). 6) Implement error boundaries and proper error handling for all async operations. RECOMMEND: Start over with security-first architecture - current code has fundamental flaws that cannot be patched incrementally.

issues: CRITICAL: Token storage vulnerability - Salesforce OAuth tokens and CSRF tokens stored in sessionStorage are vulnerable to XSS attacks. Must use httpOnly cookies with Secure and SameSite flags for session tokens, or implement a secure backend token proxy.

CRITICAL: Incomplete CSRF validation - validateCSRF function is truncated/incomplete with missing return statement and session validation logic, rendering CSRF protection non-functional. This allows state-changing operations without proper verification.

CRITICAL: CSP configuration weakness - Content Security Policy allows 'unsafe-inline' via empty script-src directive and DOMPurify fallback completely bypasses sanitization if library fails to load, creating XSS attack vectors.
data.feedback:
The implementation has multiple severe security vulnerabilities that must be addressed before deployment:

1. **Token Storage (CRITICAL)**: Move all authentication tokens to httpOnly cookies managed by backend. Never store OAuth tokens in sessionStorage. Implement: `Set-Cookie: sf_session=<token>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=3600`. If frontend needs token access, use a backend proxy endpoint.

2. **CSRF Protection (CRITICAL)**: Complete the validateCSRF function with proper validation logic: verify token exists, matches server-side token, hasn't expired, and is tied to the user session. Add server-side validation for all state-changing operations. Example: `if (!token || token !== serverToken || isExpired(token)) return false;`

3. **CSP Hardening (CRITICAL)**: Remove 'unsafe-inline' by implementing nonce-based CSP. Add to headers: `Content-Security-Policy: script-src 'nonce-<random>'; connect-src 'self' https://api.salesforce.com`. Fix DOMPurify fallback to reject content instead of bypassing: `if (!window.DOMPurify) throw new Error('Sanitizer required');`

4. **Add Missing Security Features**: Implement token refresh logic (check expiry at 80% lifetime and refresh), rate limiting (max 10 requests/minute per user), authentication state verification before API calls, and proper error boundaries with secure error logging (no sensitive data in logs).

5. **Input Validation**: Add comprehensive input validation for all user data before Salesforce API calls using allowlists for field names and strict type checking.

Estimated fix time: 8-12 hours for proper security implementation.

issues: CRITICAL: Session token stored in plain cookies without HttpOnly flag - vulnerable to XSS attacks. CSRF token generation is client-side only and can be manipulated. Authentication state is client-side managed without server-side validation.

CRITICAL: CSP allows 'unsafe-inline' styles enabling CSS injection attacks. No input sanitization/XSS protection for dynamic content. Missing SRI for external font resources creates supply chain attack vector.

HIGH: Rate limiting is client-side only (APIManager.requestCount) and easily bypassed. CSP connect-src only allows login.salesforce.com but production instances use instance.salesforce.com domains. Token refresh uses fixed 48min interval ignoring actual server expiry.
data.feedback: Immediate fixes required: 1) Move authentication to server-side with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies and server-generated CSRF tokens validated on each request. 2) Remove 'unsafe-inline' from CSP, use nonces/hashes for inline styles, add XSS sanitization library (DOMPurify) for all dynamic content, add SRI hashes to font imports. 3) Implement server-side rate limiting (token bucket algorithm), update CSP connect-src to '*.salesforce.com' or specific instance domains, parse token expiry from OAuth response and schedule refresh dynamically. 4) Add error boundaries, implement OAuth state parameter validation, use 'https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/callback' for proper OAuth flow. 5) Add session timeout with server-side validation. Code is fundamentally insecure for production use.

data.note: The code provides only basic HTML/CSS structure for the IntegrationsSettingsSection UI skeleton. Missing critical components: complete modal implementations (SalesforceConnectModal and SyncConfigurationModal are not present), all backend OAuth 2.0 authentication logic, token encryption/storage, field mapping configuration system, actual sync engine, conflict resolution implementation, database operations, and JavaScript functionality. The code is approximately 5-10% complete - it shows the visual layout but lacks all functional requirements.

blocking_issues: Missing closing tags: HTML structure is incomplete - div tags for integration-card and integrations-section appear unclosed
Hardcoded credentials: 'YOUR_SALESFORCE_CLIENT_ID' and 'renzo-secret-key-32-chars-long' must not be in client-side code
Security vulnerability: Encryption key exposed in client-side JavaScript makes encryption ineffective
OAuth popup polling: Current implementation can fail silently with cross-origin restrictions; no timeout mechanism
IndexedDB Promise handling: Using deprecated transaction.complete pattern without proper error handling
No ARIA labels: Integration cards, buttons, and interactive elements lack accessibility attributes
Missing viewport meta tag: Cannot verify mobile responsiveness without HTML head
Sync operation has no timeout: Long-running sync can hang indefinitely
Missing close button on modals - users cannot dismiss modals without clicking specific action buttons, violating accessibility and UX best practices
No keyboard navigation support - modals and interactive elements lack aria-labels, role attributes, and keyboard event handlers (ESC to close, Tab navigation)
Fixed sidebar breaks mobile layout - sidebar has fixed 240px width and position:fixed with no responsive breakpoints, making content unusable on mobile devices
Incomplete HTML - modal div with class 'mo' is cut off mid-tag, preventing page from rendering properly
No error states displayed - integration card shows 'Not Connected' but provides no explanation or troubleshooting guidance
Color contrast failures - #666 text on #F7F4EF background (3.6:1) fails WCAG AA standard (4.5:1 minimum) for body text
No loading/disabled states on buttons - users can click 'Authorize' multiple times during async operations, potentially causing duplicate requests
Missing closing tag - HTML structure has unclosed `<div>` before script section
